entries.title: errno
entries.description: When a system call or library function fails (usually by returning -1 or NULL) it stores a reason in `errno`. It is only meaningful right after a call that reported failure: a successful call may change it. Turn it into text with `strerror` or `perror`; print errors to `stderr`.
mistakes: Reading `errno` after a call that succeeded.
Another call (even `printf`) changing it before you read it.

entries.title: strerror
entries.description: `strerror(errno)` gives a message such as "No such file or directory". The returned string must not be modified.

entries.title: exit
entries.summary: End the program at once with a status.
entries.description: Flushes and closes the stdio streams and ends the process. `status` 0 (or `EXIT_SUCCESS`) means success; non-zero (`EXIT_FAILURE` is 1) means failure and is what the shell sees in `$?`. Returning `n` from `main` is the same as `exit(n)`.

entries.title: getenv
entries.description: Returns a pointer to the value or NULL if the variable is not set. Do not modify the string: copy it first (for instance before `strtok`).

details.name: PATH
details.text: directories separated by `:`, searched in order when you run a command

entries.example:
const char *home = getenv("HOME");
if (home == NULL) home = "/";
mistakes: Using the result without checking for NULL.
